issue-4403: Is the byte order mark at the start of CSV exports deliberate?
Opened by warehouse-etl-ken on 2026-10-20

Our Python loader reads the first column of every Ledgerline CSV as `\ufeffDate`
instead of `Date`. A hex viewer shows the bytes EF BB BF at the start of the
file. Is that on purpose

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Yes, it's deliberate: src/export/csv.ts prepends a UTF-8 byte order mark (EF BB BF) by default, since spreadsheet apps use it to detect UTF-8 when a CSV is opened directly. There's already a `bom` option on `writeCsv` to turn it off if a caller needs plain UTF-8, but the exported endpoints currently use the default. Opening with `utf-8-sig` on your end is the right workaround, and the behavior isn't expected to change since it's there for spreadsheet compatibility.
